# A08 · Target screening and dated bands {#a08-target-ranges}

A measured band can intersect a target briefly, more than once, or exactly at a turning point. We compared [`findTargets()`](help/findTargets.html) with independent annual stellar samples and a separate line-segment intersection calculation. For solar and lunar limits, the reference evaluates January obliquity and the local parallax term for every integer year. All 129 assertions passed.

**Stellar membership.** In a 30–42 CE search, a narrow band around a turning point for Sirius returned *35–35 CE* and *38–39 CE* after rounding the interpolated boundaries to years. The exact annual maximum gave one contact in 36 CE. The study also tested magnitude inclusion and exclusion, one-year searches, catalogue identifiers and aliases, and the pairing of colours and styles with their targets. The implementation treats stellar differences within 0.0000001° of an edge as a contact. The reference shares the stellar ephemeris. This study validates selection and aggregation; stellar positions at subannual extrema remain outside this model.

**Solar and lunar bounds.** At 50° N over astronomical years −3400 to −3100 the southern major lunar limits span approximately −30.08° to −30.05°. Annual local bounds include both endpoints for one-year, short, modern and prehistoric ranges. Spherical inversion of the returned orbit coordinates recovered their input declinations.

Candidate selection uses unrounded declinations. Two-decimal limits are display values. Solar zenith/anti-zenith screening uses the archaeological period and requires a reachable passage. The spatial-equinox candidate uses the rising and setting solutions from the endpoint epochs; this particular candidate does not claim to enclose every intermediate year's terrain midpoint. [Download the A08 scripts and results](archives/A08.zip).
